item.title: Indonesians brave choking smoke to pray for rain as country battles wildfires
item.description: Huge blazes in central and western regions of Indonesia have scorched wide areas of forests and peatland, creating a choking haze that blanketed some cities.

item.title: This scientist uses light to perform smarter, cleaner chemistry
item.description: To create the molecules we need to help us grow food or make fuel, we rely on chemical reactions — and lots of energy. One scientist may have a "brighter" approach, controlling chemistry with light.

item.title: Lab-grown organoids are living longer — offering new insight into the human brain
item.description: A study in the journal Nature sets a new record for the lifespan of lab-grown cells called organoids. These clusters of human cells in petri dishes are used as models of the human brain.
item.content:encoded: A study in the journal Nature sets a new record for the lifespan of lab-grown cells called organoids. These clusters of human cells in petri dishes are used as models of the human brain.

item.title: This week in science: A new black hole star, exercises for dementia, and winter shrews
item.description: NPR's science podcast Short Wave talks about a new type of black hole star, the types of exercise linked to lowered dementia risk, and the wintry adaptations of the long-clawed shrew.

item.title: As USS Lincoln heads home, mental health experts tally the stressors of life at sea
item.description: The USS Abraham Lincoln is now on its way home after spending nine months at sea. Experts weigh in on the mental health challenges of prolonged confinement and isolation aboard an aircraft carrier.

item.title: Federal government thins the herds of wild horses in Colorado
item.description: U.S. officials say the ever-growing population of wild horses that roam federal lands in Colorado is depleting natural resources. But some activists say efforts to remove the horses are inhumane.
